definitions.definition: Ttor = reals/(2*pi*integers), with normalized measure dx/(2*pi); spatial products and integrals are on this domain.
For an integrable periodic f, Fourier(f)(k)=hat f(k)=(2*pi)^(-1) integral_0^(2*pi) f(x) exp(-i*k*x) dx; the transform extends to distributions by duality.

For every real s, H^s(Ttor) is the completion of trigonometric polynomials with ||f||_(H^s)^2=sum_(k in Z) <k>^(2*s)|hat f(k)|^2, <k>=(1+k^2)^(1/2). Negative spaces are interpreted as distributions. Homogeneous norms on zero-mean distributions are ||f||_(dot H^s)^2=sum_(k!=0)|k|^(2*s)|hat f(k)|^2. Real means hat f(-k)=conjugate(hat f(k)); mean zero means hat f(0)=0.

L2=H^0(Ttor), with ||f||_2^2=(2*pi)^(-1) integral |f|^2 dx. More generally L^p uses the same normalized measure; L^infinity is essential supremum. Sequence ell^2 uses counting measure on Z (or Z\{0} when specified). Time suprema use continuous representatives; derivative norms are essential suprema.

definitions.definition: KdV is u_t+u_xxx=(1/2)*partial_x(u^2), u(0)=u0. An exact solution on [0,T] with H^gamma data means the unique real mean-zero C([0,T];H^gamma(Ttor)) distributional solution obtained by smooth approximation. This describes the convention and asserts no existence. For such a solution write v(t)=S_(-t)u(t), and M=1+sup_[0,T]||v(t)||_(H^gamma).

inputs.statement: For the real mean-zero normalized 2*pi-periodic source equation U_t=U U_x+U_xxx, use the source twisted coefficients y_k(t)=exp(i*k^3*t) hat U(k,t), k!=0, with ||y||_(dot H^s)^2=sum_(k!=0)|k|^(2*s)|y_k|^2. for s>=0, finite T_s>0, initial dot H^s datum y0 and an upper bound B0 for its L2 norm, the source Galerkin flows have sup_[0,T_s] dot H^s norm bounded by a constant depending only on s,T_s,||y0||_(dot H^s),B0, uniformly in Galerkin dimension. For s>0 a subsequence converges to a distributional limiting solution with the same bound (the limiting statement uses strong L^p_t H^sigma convergence for 0<sigma<s and 1<p<infinity and weak-star L^infinity_t dot H^s convergence). The uniqueness and continuity claims for s>1/2 and for 0<s<=1/2 make this solution unique, C([0,T_s];dot H^s), L2 conserving and Lipschitz continuous in the initial dot H^s data. At s=0, for s=0 there is a unique C([0,T_s];dot H^0) solution obtained by smooth approximation and Lipschitz continuous in the initial data. For the two-flow estimate, for theta in (-1,0], if ||y0||_2+||z0||_2<=B, then their two source twisted flows satisfy sup_[0,T_s]||y-z||_(dot H^theta)<=C'(B,theta)*C_B(theta)^(T_s)*||y0-z0||_(dot H^theta). All these claims concern the source equation and its twist, not the target sign convention.

output.statement: There is A=A(T,gamma,R)<infinity such that every real mean-zero initial datum f0 in H^gamma with ||f0||_(H^gamma)<=R has a unique exact KdV solution in the convention D012 and sup_[0,T]||u(t)||_(H^gamma)<=A. Smooth initial data give smooth solutions, with the same H^gamma bound. Thus the twisted v=S_(-t)u obeys M<=1+A uniformly on this ball. For any B>0, two real mean-zero initial L2 data with norm sum <=B have flows satisfying sup_[0,T]||u-tilde u||_2<=C(T,B)||u0-tilde u0||_2. In particular real mean-zero Fourier polynomial approximations to H^gamma data converge in C([0,T];L2) to this solution.

argument.text: H001–H003 give T>0, 0<gamma<=1 and R>0. Fix f0 under L1. Reflection and sign preserve each Fourier magnitude: the source initial datum -f0(-x) has coefficient -hat f0(-k). For a mean-zero datum and s>=0, ||f||_(dot H^s)<=||f||_(H^s)<=2^(s/2)||f||_(dot H^s), since |k|<=<k><=sqrt(2)|k| at k!=0. Apply E001 with s=gamma, T_s=T, B0=R and initial homogeneous norm bounded by R. The source Galerkin bound passes to its limiting flow by its Galerkin and limiting-solution clauses, and the source uniqueness/continuity clause covers gamma>1/2 and 0<gamma<=1/2. Thus obtain U with a uniform homogeneous bound depending only on T,gamma,R.

produces.statement: The source flow U exists, is unique and continuous in dot H^gamma, and has a bound depending only on T,gamma,R.

argument.text: Define u(t,x)=-U(t,-x). For smooth functions u_t=-U_t, u_x=U_x and u_xxx=U_xxx at (t,-x), so u_t+u_xxx=-U U_x=u u_x=(1/2)partial_x(u^2). The same change of variables in test functions proves the distributional identity for the limiting solution. The inverse reflection gives uniqueness. Sobolev norm comparison from S001 yields a common bound A(T,gamma,R); limits obey it since each finite Fourier norm sum passes to the limit and the full positive norm sum is the supremum of its finite sums. Continuity in H^gamma extends an almost-everywhere bound to every time. Smooth data are in every dot H^s; apply E001 at each positive integer s and identify the flows by uniqueness, giving smoothness sufficient for all later calculations.

produces.statement: For f0 under L1, u is the unique exact target-sign solution and sup ||u||_(H^gamma)<=A(T,gamma,R); smooth f0 gives a smooth solution.

argument.text: S_t is a Fourier multiplier of modulus one, hence preserves every H^s norm, reality and zero mean. Therefore the exact twist v(t)=S_(-t)u(t) has M=1+sup||u||_(H^gamma)<=1+A(T,gamma,R). Discharge L1 and quantify over all f0 in the stated ball.

For arbitrary B>0 and two real mean-zero L2 initial data a0,b0 with norm sum <=B, apply E001's L2 existence and two-flow Lipschitz clauses at theta=0, T_s=T. Denote the resulting target-sign physical flows u_a,u_b, using the reflection already proved. The source twist and reflection preserve their normalized L2 distance, so sup_[0,T]||u_a-u_b||_2<=C(T,B)||a0-b0||_2. For any real mean-zero datum d0 in H^gamma, its real Fourier polynomial truncations tend to d0 in L2, and the same Lipschitz estimate shows convergence of their flows in C([0,T];L2). The limit agrees with the H^gamma flow by uniqueness. This proves the smooth-approximation convention and the full two-flow assertion.
